original_question: If X is a consonant T0 space, is its Hoare power space PH(X) also consonant?
target_in_paper: Question 6.16 (Section 6): For a consonant T0 space X, is PH(X) also consonant?
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the right hypothesis (X is a consonant T0 space), the right construction (the Hoare power space PH(X)), and the right property being asked about (whether PH(X) is consonant). It also correctly avoids drifting to the neighboring Question 6.15 about the Smyth power space PS(X).
missing_details: State the universal quantifier explicitly: the paper asks whether for every consonant T0 space X, the conclusion holds.
Define the Hoare power space exactly as used in the paper: PH(X)=PH(Γ(X) \ {∅})=(Γ(X) \ {∅}, υ(Γ(X) \ {∅})), where Γ(X) is the set of closed subsets of X and υ is the lower Vietoris topology.
Specify the lower Vietoris subbasic opens: for U in O(X), 3U={A in Γ(X) \ {∅} : A ∩ U ≠ ∅}.

Define consonance so the question is stand-alone: a T0 space Y is consonant if every Scott-open family F ⊆ O(Y) can be written as F = ⋃_{i∈I} Φ(K_i), where each K_i is a nonempty compact saturated subset of Y and Φ(K)={U∈O(Y): K⊆U}.
Make clear that no additional hypotheses such as sobriety, local compactness, core compactness, or first-countability are part of this specific open question.
Relevant nearby context omitted from the draft: the paper notes that PH(X) is always sober, so the issue is preservation of consonance, not sobriety, under the Hoare power-space construction.
refined_question: For every consonant T0 space X, let PH(X)=PH(Γ(X) \ {∅})=(Γ(X) \ {∅}, υ(Γ(X) \ {∅})) be the Hoare (lower) power space of X, where Γ(X) is the set of closed subsets of X and υ is the lower Vietoris topology generated by the subbasic sets 3U={A∈Γ(X) \ {∅}: A∩U≠∅} for U∈O(X). Must PH(X) be consonant? Here a T0 space Y is consonant if every Scott-open family F⊆O(Y) is of the form F=⋃_{i∈I} Φ(K_i), where each K_i is a nonempty compact saturated subset of Y and Φ(K)={U∈O(Y): K⊆U}.
equivalent_formulation: Since PH(X) is always sober, this is equivalently the question whether, for every consonant T0 space X, the Scott topology on O(PH(X)) has a basis consisting of Scott-open filters.
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the open problem recorded as Question 6.16 in Section 6. The surrounding context first defines consonance, then states Theorem 6.14 on equivalent formulations of consonance, then recalls Brecht and Kawai’s commutativity result for upper and lower power spaces, and immediately asks Question 6.16. Section 2 supplies the exact meaning of PH(X) as the Hoare/lower power space. Because the paper separately states that PH(X) is always sober, the paper-faithful alternate formulation via Scott-open filters is available, but the official target remains the narrowly stated Question 6.16 rather than any broader preservation problem.
